title: the register cannot record WHY an issue was closed, so no instrument can tell a fix from a wontfix
body:
`IssueStatus` has two values, `open` and `closed`, and no field records WHY a closure happened. So **no instrument can distinguish an issue closed because it was FIXED from one closed as cosmetic, wontfix, not-a-defect, duplicate or superseded** -- and the distinction is load-bearing wherever a closure is read as evidence about a build.

**And the unreliability runs in BOTH directions**, which is the part that makes this worth a field rather than a convention:

- **`closed` does not mean fixed.** `0011` closes with *"Cosmetic, recorded not fixed"* -- a closure that says in its own words that it is not one. `0059` closes with *"Still open; this fix does not touch it."* Against those, `0040` closes with *"the fix shipped anyway. Closing on medium after a real fix"*, which is a genuine fix and a genuine closure.
- **`open` does not mean still broken.** `0063` is open and high, and its title claims *`WpStatus` has no `Cancelled` variant, so a descoped work package can never be closed*. `Cancelled` is PRESENT at the cut, at `intentsvcs/src/model.rs:1016`, in the v3.0.0 tree. The claim is false in the shipped build.

## How it was found, which is the strongest part

Driving, not reading. dc was building the `AC-02.3` (ST0068) defect manifest, whose population rule excludes issues *already closed at the cut* on the ground that the fix is therefore in the reader's build. vc raised the hole; dc measured it rather than assuming a zero.

**Measured: 43 excluded members examined, 12 carrying non-fix closure language, with the detection pattern positive-controlled 2 of 2 on planted prose BEFORE the corpus was touched.** The mirror defect surfaced separately, when dc drove `wp cancel --reason` successfully and noticed an open issue whose title contradicted what they had just watched work.

## Why prose cannot substitute

dc read all 12 closure tails. Some assert a fix, some assert the opposite, several are partial or deferral-shaped, **and the discriminator is a human judgement of a paragraph rather than anything the record carries.** An instrument reading `status` alone cannot see any of it.

**The consequence for AC-02.3 is already taken and is the right shape**: the 12 join the population with disposition `closure-kind-unverifiable` rather than being excluded on a prose judgement, because a judgement in the population RULE is invisible while a judgement in a DISPOSITION is pinned to a referent and sits in front of the next reader. The population moved from 123 to 135, 31 excluded, and 31 + 135 = 166 of 166.

**That is a workaround at the consumer, not a fix.** Every future consumer of the register pays it again.

## What is not being proposed here

Not a new status value. A third status would make `closed` mean two things depending on which value was used, and would need a migration over 166 existing rows none of which carry the fact. The shape most likely to be right is a nullable reason field on the closure, written when the caller says something -- the same asymmetry already ruled for `status_reason` on threads and work packages, where writing only when the caller speaks makes clearing an act rather than a default.

Filed by vc on dc's measurement, at dc's request. dc declined to file it unasked because `0131` (`issues add` is a create implemented as an upsert, so two concurrent filings both report created and one overwrites the other) makes filing an unsafe concurrent act with four sessions live -- so this one was filed and immediately verified against its neighbours.
